transcript: alright let's keep this going Edinburgh Fringe reviews part 4 I saw a Scooby Doo parody a Best Man's speech gone wrong and a queer musical comedy about Renaissance artists Solve It Squad is from the company Tin Can Bros I believe this is an offshoot from some of the folks behind Team Starkid it's essentially a Scooby Doo parody where the team is all grown up and they have to get the gang back together I found it incredibly funny and it's a great example of what can come when you have a group that is so clearly on the same page artistically there's an almost effortless quality to it where the comedy is very sharp but you can also tell that a lot of these bits just came about organically from having such a clear idea of what they were doing that they had the comfort to play around within it Pop Off, Michelangelo! this is a new musical comedy that portrays the friendship and rivalry between Renaissance artists Michelangelo and Leonardo da Vinci but through a very queer lens one is getting a lot of buzz at the festival I'd heard a lot of hype about it beforehand and so I rearranged my schedule to see it comedically I absolutely think it lives up to the hype all of the jokes in both the dialogue and the lyrics are incredibly clever I was constantly laughing out loud The rest of it, like the music and the story, I felt a little bit like okay like maybe we've seen stuff like this before but it all worked very well as a vehicle for the comedy finally Best Man this is a one man play from Ireland where the whole concept is that you are essentially watching a best man speech going off the rails as he's kind of in crisis about still being single in his thirties as he goes along he casts the audience members as different people in the crowd at the wedding which is a lot of fun I don't always love cringe comedy and I think that's part partly because with a lot of cringe comedy you kind of get ahead of them and you start anticipating that the worst thing is gonna happen and then it does but I think this show is actually really good at keeping us on our toes so a lot of the cringiest things that happen are actually surprises and so we can kind of go along for the ride and laugh at it I was also really impressed at how they managed to sustain this concept for a full 50 minutes without straining our suspension of disbelief
